His sense of duty for America led him to this decision, and I have no doubt he will continue to serve the American people for years to come. Here’s what I need to say to you right now: Our main responsibility is to elect someone who is committed to democracy, justice, and a healthy, livable planet. Donald Trump has told us clearly that he wants a dictatorship from Day One, will do away with our environmental regulations and give free reign to Big Oil. We cannot allow that to happen and that means voting. Sitting it out or voting for a third party candidate means voting for fascism. The upcoming November election remains our most critical — and potentially our _last_ chance — to take decisive climate action to prevent the climate crisis from escalating to climate catastrophe. We cannot afford four years of damage done to our air, our water, and our health with Donald Trump and his Big Oil allies in the White House. We need a brave president who will lead us into a clean energy future and hold corporate polluters accountable for the harm they cause to our communities and our planet. But let me be clear: This isn't just about who sits in the White House. Bold climate policy is being set in state legislatures, city councils, and county boards all across the country. So much progress has been made. We mustn’t allow it to be undone. Every half degree of warming we can prevent will save millions of lives. Down-ballot races may not make national headlines, but they are hugely important and can act as a firewall, protecting us in the event of a worst-case scenario in November. Your support of my Climate PAC and our down-ballot races across the country is invaluable and strategic. This piece is going to upset some, but I'm hopeful you'll read all the way through before passing judgement. Let me start by stating that I believe President Biden was right to withdraw, that VP Harris is the best chance we have to beat Trump this November, [and that she will win if she upholds justice on these three pillars](https://substack.com/redirect/97c5d284-1db8-4308-b0ca-9d28557800e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Now let me get to the point. Right now, the Democratic Party has a broken primary system that is hurting our democracy, and this simply cannot continue. A popular tweet that goes viral every election season goes something like this:
> At 55% voter turnout, Republicans win.
> At 60% voter turnout, Democrats win.
> At 65% voter turnout, there's an Obama-like rout.
> At 70% voter turnout, there's no longer a Republican party.
> Stop complaining, vote blue no matter who, and let's save our democracy.
I do not know who first coined this tweet, but its message is clear--the more people vote, the stronger our democracy remains, the more robustly our republic withstands challenges to its existence, and the more accurately our government reflects the will of the people. All great ideals.
And while I don't know many Democrats who would disagree with the above in principle, when it comes to practical application, the narrative shifts and primaries are shouted down. The fact is, "_vote blue no matter who_ " is a hollow phrase when the "blue" isn't chosen via a robust primary. We already know [the Republican party is anti-democracy](https://substack.com/redirect/20ba56a9-2460-4ed7-8187-e3c91ce9b967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and that's why it is so much more critical that the Democratic party does everything it can to be pro democracy at every opportunity.
President Biden is being hailed as a selfless patriot for withdrawing from reelection. But we must acknowledge that his decision to do so at the last possible minute and then immediately endorse VP Harris to the presidency is--as a strategy to foster democracy--unsustainable and problematic. This approach is not how we strengthen democracy, not how we maximize turnout, and not how we ensure our elected leaders reflect the will of the people. As always, I bring the receipts to back up what I mean.
**Let 's Address This.**
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2550223&post_id=146889230&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ2ODg5MjMwLCJpYXQiOjE3MjE2ODYyMzgsImV4cCI6MTcyNDI3ODIzOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI1NTAyMjMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.fWeOdqkzurAKKXmzqM1lFFUtiPKMTnWQM18i4o4DrCA)
## How We Got Here
Back in 2020 President Biden ran for President on the promise of being a "_bridge President_ " to a younger generation, [suggesting he would only serve one term](https://substack.com/redirect/b00eeea5-1273-4657-93c6-0820d8a6b02f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and then pass the torch. At numerous rallies he loudly [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/92edfccd-21c9-4d64-a966-9f6755305617?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),
> Look, I view myself as a bridge, not as anything else. I view myself as a transition candidate.
It was with that explicit expectation that a [monsoon of young voters](https://substack.com/redirect/09a9b17b-ffce-4da4-b4b4-3c54afd3e9a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) helped him cross the finish line, earning 7 million more votes than Donald Trump. But when it became clear that President Biden had no intention of stepping down, those who suggested he follow through on his campaign promise were dismissed, decried, and denounced. Even as poll after poll showed that [Biden's support among the young people who helped him win in 2020 was all but gone](https://substack.com/redirect/67945a18-dec4-4dec-ab68-08cd8f5abb42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), those who believed Biden should withdraw were shouted down. If you don't believe me, simply glance at the onslaught of critical responses to any elected or candidate who suggested Biden should withdraw. Here's a mere snapshot of the hundreds of angry responses Democratic candidate Adam Frisch got [for calling on Biden to withdraw on July 2](https://substack.com/redirect/46160c6f-ad39-46a7-9941-078b441c79ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d64c9b85-3aeb-49f3-bf6e-910ebab5d06e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Overwhelmingly negative responses to Adam Frisch for suggesting President Biden withdraw
Known moderates like Rep Adam Schiff, Senator Mark Warner, and Senator Chuck Schumer all received similar backlash for suggesting President Biden withdraw. In hindsight, Frisch was right. As of the writing of this article, the Harris for President campaign has raised a historic $81M in just 24 hours. People are excited about a younger candidate, a female candidate, a Black candidate, an Asian candidate--people are excited about the next generation Biden promised he would be a bridge towards.
But the abuse Frisch and many others received who simply wanted Biden to uphold his campaign promise, should not have happened. The abuse many received simply for calling for a robust primary, should not have been received. By staying in as long as he did, despite promising otherwise when elected, President Biden denied the American people of a robust primary that would have given us a stronger candidate and party. And yes, that candidate may well have still been Kamala Harris, but it is critical to realize the ends don't justify the means here. The primary process allows voters to have their voice heard and their candidate given a shot. Denying that process alienates voters in the general, and as the data below shows, every percent makes a critical difference to ensuring we maintain a healthy sustainable democracy.

## How Valuable Is a Robust Primary Anyway?
In a word, priceless. If we truly care about a thriving democracy, we must champion robust primaries at every opportunity because it is the best way to maximize voter turnout for the general and stave off fascist takeover attempts like Project 2025. Recall the aforementioned tweet about turnout and consider these historical facts.
**In 2008 the Democratic party had a robust 10 candidate primary.** Rather than anointing any candidate, Americans got to see a dynamic young candidate from Illinois make his case. The end result? President Obama made history as the nation's first Black major party nominee for President, made history as the nation's first Black President, winning by an astounding 9.5 million votes, and decimated the Republican nominee McCain 365-173 in the Electoral count. [Voter turnout was at a historic 61.6%](https://substack.com/redirect/45cd1815-19da-4339-849d-5954be5beecd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a level that won Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ff7dd24-976f-4d0b-a92b-a5fb3aba16bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Democratic presidential candidates in 2007. Credit: Justin Hayworth-Pool/Getty Images
**In 2016 the Democratic Party cleared the field for Hillary Clinton.** To be sure, I believe she likely would still have been the nominee were there a comprehensive and robust primary. But we weren't afforded that. My statement is not opinion. [The DNC itself acknowledged in 2016 it unfairly favored Hillary Clinton](https://substack.com/redirect/8a4de8d5-9f61-48b1-b230-a6a82b5a7d60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). As the Party establishment coalesced around Clinton, it left many Democratic primary voters upset at an unfair fight. And in the general, despite winning the popular vote by 3 million votes, Clinton lost the Electoral count 227-332. [Voter turnout dropped to 59.2%](https://substack.com/redirect/45cd1815-19da-4339-849d-5954be5beecd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a drop that cost Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate.
I want to emphasize this key point. A 2.4% drop in turnout was the difference between controlling all of the White House, House, and Senate, and controlling none of them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a71877c-bb42-458c-9e99-ce0598fc39fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: CBS News
**In 2020 the Democratic Party began a robust 28 candidate primary** (though somewhat hindered as Obama eventually [helped clear the field for Biden](https://substack.com/redirect/168f1f34-ca8a-49de-b1d5-2a71ffdbc698?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). Still, the size of the primary better pressure tested Biden and forced him to rise to the occasion to win. Biden won by 7 million votes and won the electoral count 306-232. Moreover, that primary helped provide data and insight into selecting a VP candidate that would most strengthen the ticket, i.e. Kamala Harris. [Voter turnout was at a historic 66%](https://substack.com/redirect/dc6fa619-db76-4c3f-835a-084640de0625?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a level that once again won Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0857783-6522-41d4-9f1f-04152ddfbd72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: Politico
The ACA, the Infrastructure Bill, the CHIPS Act, and countless more critical life saving pieces of legislation, all made possible by Presidents elected via a robust primary that maximized voter turnout and decimated Republican opposition at the ballot box. That is how critical robust primaries are to not only protecting our democracy, but to advancing the causes of justice in the United States.
Now, as the party coalesces around Harris for President, the lack of a robust primary in 2024 means we lack the critical data, tested polls, and tested campaign trails that we would have had when selecting the best possible VP candidate to strengthen the Democratic ticket. My fear is the lack of a robust primary in 2024 risks a result like that of 2016--and given the fascist Project 2025--a loss this time could quite literally mean the end of our democracy as we know it. We cannot allow that to happen.
## Listen To Young People
Preventing fascism means listening to young people. The Democratic Party cannot merely talk about protecting democracy, we must act on proven models to maximize voter turnout, strengthen our democracy, protect our republic, and ensure our elected representatives truly reflect the will of the people. In particular, young people who helped Democrats win in 2020. After being promised a bridge presidency in 2020, Gen-Z has made no secret about [their disappointment in lack of options for President](https://substack.com/redirect/63cf3d6f-dc67-49f2-b61d-9bc9daa70224?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2024. Given their massively growing influence, it's unwise to ignore Gen-Z.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3ffc54-b43d-46c7-bb7f-cfba39dbc2c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: Circle at Tufts - Tufts University
It's easy to understand why. Gen-Z voters are drowning in student debt, unable to afford out of control home prices, and devastated about the climate crisis. Few demographics better understand the struggles of working Americans today than do Gen-Z Americans, making it no surprise that they are [turned off by the 2024 election](https://substack.com/redirect/4b1cf18f-b619-480b-a611-1590214b7882?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The 2020 election proved that when you inspire young voters, you win across the board. Thus, it behooves the Democratic Party to listen to our next generation of voters and leaders to ensure Democrats earn that vote this November, and beyond.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..leFCiJzFzTJr-Vl1cDNCmMkQyMrRBBMzqPl5FdncJrs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=146889230)
## In Conclusion
I felt compelled to write this piece because my commitment is to uphold justice above all else--including above party lines--because we can only form a more perfect Union on the tenets of absolute justice, and by maximizing the number of people we include in the democratic process. I was shocked to learn that with Biden's withdrawal, this is the first time since 1976 that the Presidential ballot does _not_ have a Bush, Clinton, or Biden on the ballot. In a functioning democracy, three families should not dominate the most powerful office in the land for half a century--yet here we are.
The data is clear. When we have high voter turnout, Democrats win. Republicans know this, and it's one reason they've repeatedly voted to block voting rights legislation. Let me start by stating that I believe President Biden was right to withdraw, that VP Harris is the best chance we have to beat Trump this November, . Now let me get to the point. Right now, the Democratic Party has a broken primary system that is hurting our democracy, and this simply cannot continue. A popular tweet that goes viral every election season goes something like this: At 55% voter turnout, Republicans win. At 60% voter turnout, Democrats win. At 65% voter turnout, there's an Obama-like rout. At 70% voter turnout, there's no longer a Republican party. Stop complaining, vote blue no matter who, and let's save our democracy. I do not know who first coined this tweet, but its message is clear--the more people vote, the stronger our democracy remains, the more robustly our republic withstands challenges to its existence, and the more accurately our government reflects the will of the people. All great ideals. And while I don't know many Democrats who would disagree with the above in principle, when it comes to practical application, the narrative shifts and primaries are shouted down. The fact is, "vote blue no matter who " is a hollow phrase when the "blue" isn't chosen via a robust primary. We already know , and that's why it is so much more critical that the Democratic party does everything it can to be pro democracy at every opportunity. President Biden is being hailed as a selfless patriot for withdrawing from reelection. But we must acknowledge that his decision to do so at the last possible minute and then immediately endorse VP Harris to the presidency is--as a strategy to foster democracy--unsustainable and problematic. This approach is not how we strengthen democracy, not how we maximize turnout, and not how we ensure our elected leaders reflect the will of the people. As always, I bring the receipts to back up what I mean. Let 's Address This. How We Got Here Back in 2020 President Biden ran for President on the promise of being a "bridge President " to a younger generation, and then pass the torch. At numerous rallies he loudly , Look, I view myself as a bridge, not as anything else. I view myself as a transition candidate. It was with that explicit expectation that a helped him cross the finish line, earning 7 million more votes than Donald Trump. But when it became clear that President Biden had no intention of stepping down, those who suggested he follow through on his campaign promise were dismissed, decried, and denounced. Even as poll after poll showed that , those who believed Biden should withdraw were shouted down. If you don't believe me, simply glance at the onslaught of critical responses to any elected or candidate who suggested Biden should withdraw. Here's a mere snapshot of the hundreds of angry responses Democratic candidate Adam Frisch got . | | ---|---|--- Overwhelmingly negative responses to Adam Frisch for suggesting President Biden withdraw Known moderates like Rep Adam Schiff, Senator Mark Warner, and Senator Chuck Schumer all received similar backlash for suggesting President Biden withdraw. In hindsight, Frisch was right. As of the writing of this article, the Harris for President campaign has raised a historic $81M in just 24 hours. People are excited about a younger candidate, a female candidate, a Black candidate, an Asian candidate--people are excited about the next generation Biden promised he would be a bridge towards. But the abuse Frisch and many others received who simply wanted Biden to uphold his campaign promise, should not have happened. The abuse many received simply for calling for a robust primary, should not have been received. By staying in as long as he did, despite promising otherwise when elected, President Biden denied the American people of a robust primary that would have given us a stronger candidate and party. And yes, that candidate may well have still been Kamala Harris, but it is critical to realize the ends don't justify the means here. The primary process allows voters to have their voice heard and their candidate given a shot. Denying that process alienates voters in the general, and as the data below shows, every percent makes a critical difference to ensuring we maintain a healthy sustainable democracy. How Valuable Is a Robust Primary Anyway? In a word, priceless. If we truly care about a thriving democracy, we must champion robust primaries at every opportunity because it is the best way to maximize voter turnout for the general and stave off fascist takeover attempts like Project 2025. Recall the aforementioned tweet about turnout and consider these historical facts. In 2008 the Democratic party had a robust 10 candidate primary. Rather than anointing any candidate, Americans got to see a dynamic young candidate from Illinois make his case. The end result? President Obama made history as the nation's first Black major party nominee for President, made history as the nation's first Black President, winning by an astounding 9.5 million votes, and decimated the Republican nominee McCain 365-173 in the Electoral count. level that won Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate. | | ---|---|--- Democratic presidential candidates in 2007. Credit: Justin Hayworth-Pool/Getty Images In 2016 the Democratic Party cleared the field for Hillary Clinton. To be sure, I believe she likely would still have been the nominee were there a comprehensive and robust primary. But we weren't afforded that. My statement is not opinion. . As the Party establishment coalesced around Clinton, it left many Democratic primary voters upset at an unfair fight. And in the general, despite winning the popular vote by 3 million votes, Clinton lost the Electoral count 227-332. drop that cost Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate. I want to emphasize this key point. A 2.4% drop in turnout was the difference between controlling all of the White House, House, and Senate, and controlling none of them. | | ---|---|--- Credit: CBS News In 2020 the Democratic Party began a robust 28 candidate primary (though somewhat hindered as Obama eventually ). Still, the size of the primary better pressure tested Biden and forced him to rise to the occasion to win. Biden won by 7 million votes and won the electoral count 306-232. Moreover, that primary helped provide data and insight into selecting a VP candidate that would most strengthen the ticket, i.e. Kamala Harris. level that once again won Democrats the White House, the House, and the Senate. | | ---|---|--- Credit: Politico The ACA, the Infrastructure Bill, the CHIPS Act, and countless more critical life saving pieces of legislation, all made possible by Presidents elected via a robust primary that maximized voter turnout and decimated Republican opposition at the ballot box. That is how critical robust primaries are to not only protecting our democracy, but to advancing the causes of justice in the United States. Now, as the party coalesces around Harris for President, the lack of a robust primary in 2024 means we lack the critical data, tested polls, and tested campaign trails that we would have had when selecting the best possible VP candidate to strengthen the Democratic ticket. My fear is the lack of a robust primary in 2024 risks a result like that of 2016--and given the fascist Project 2025--a loss this time could quite literally mean the end of our democracy as we know it. We cannot allow that to happen. Listen To Young People Preventing fascism means listening to young people. Gen-Z voters are drowning in student debt, unable to afford out of control home prices, and devastated about the climate crisis. Thus, it behooves the Democratic Party to listen to our next generation of voters and leaders to ensure Democrats earn that vote this November, and beyond. name: Alsobrooks HQ
subject: It's Your Weekly Team Alsobrooks Newsletter!
body:
Greetings #Team Alsobrooks,

Another incredible week in the books! Thank you to all our supporters who
showed up and showed out! Team Alsobrooks is growing by the minute and our
people-powered movement is ready to win this November!

Angela is proud to endorse Kamala Harris for President! Please see below
for her statement:

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1029&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

In case you missed it, here’s what’s been happening on the campaign trail
and beyond:

We had the privilege of spending a few days on the Eastern Shore last
week, visiting small businesses and speaking with community leaders and
members.

We stopped by Queen Anne’s County and spent some time with Watermen and
campaign supporters. Thank you to Captain Tyrone for showing us around the
water. As Senator, Angela will work tirelessly to increase investments
into Maryland’s fishing and crabbing industries. We look forward to coming
back!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1036&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1037&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

It was great to visit Big Mixx Salon and Phat Daddy’s BBQ in Chestertown!
Thank you to everyone who joined our meet and greet! These small
businesses represent a vibrant, growing community in Chestertown. As
Maryland’s next Senator, Angela will fight for legislation that ensures
these businesses can continue to thrive.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1038&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

Next up: Modern Stone Age Kitchen! The Modern Stone Age Kitchen is one of
Chestertown’s gems. As Senator, Angela will work to modernize the grant
process small businesses rely on and ensure businesses like the Modern
Stone Age Kitchen have the resources needed to continue serving the
Eastern Shore.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1039&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

It was a pleasure to visit the Chestertown Marina! It was great to see the
Mayor of Galena, John Carroll, and the Mayor of Chestertown, David Foster,
along with so many other Marylanders who are fired up about our campaign.
As Senator, Angela will fight to ensure our environment is always
protected from the impacts of climate change, and we look forward to being
back in Chestertown soon!

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/28895?t=1040&amount=25&akid=2059%2E52803%2EmzkhDz ][IMG]

| | Last night I was filled with pride as Tennessee became the first state to pledge all its delegates to Kamala Harris, the first woman of color to become the Democratic presidential nominee. This significant achievement is not only a testament to our unity but also a powerful statement about our dedication to progress and representation.

Tennessee Democrats are stepping up for the country and now we need to come together and step up for our home state.

**Together, we can make a HUGE change. A donation of $25 can keep this Blue momentum going here in the great state of Tennessee.**

As we fight together in the coming months to elect our first female president, we must fight tooth and nail at the local level. This election season candidates like Jesse Huseth, Luis Mata, Allie Philips, Bryan Goldberg, and Karen Reynolds each have a strong chance to turn a red district blue and take back a seat. But not without our help. These candidates represent the diverse and progressive values that Tennessee needs. They are committed to issues like healthcare, education, and economic equality, which resonate with voters across the state.

Our collective efforts here at home in Tennessee are just as crucial as our national ambitions, and together, we can make a difference.

With hope,
Ann Perry
Our Tennessee Future PAC Team

| Peter,

President Joe Biden announced he is dropping out of the race.

In his statement not to seek re-election, he reminded us all that “[T]here is nothing America can’t do - when we do it together. We just have to remember we are the United States of America.”

His decision to put country over party and personal power speaks volumes, and it sets an example of service above self. This stands in stark contrast to Jack Bergman, who reimbursed himself $44,000 in tax-payer money for food and lodging above his $174,000 salary, who voted against funding for our district while taking credit for it, and who supported the Tuberville blockade of military promotions, all to support his partisan agenda.

I know we can make a difference in Upper and Northern Michigan - together. That’s why electing leaders who will advocate for us and not for private and corporate interests–leaders who will put country over party, cooperation over division–is so important.

So, while protecting our democracy and putting country before party, let’s tackle issues impacting us here at home: the high cost of living, bringing good jobs here, protecting women’s reproductive freedoms, and advocating for veterans and military families.

| Peter,

California's agricultural industry is vital to the economy and deeply rooted in the hard work and dedication of migrant farmworkers. As the country's **#1 agricultural producer,** it’s safe to say that our country is fueled by and relies on farmworkers.

Despite their immense contributions, migrant farmworkers continue to face systemic challenges, including _inadequate access to healthcare, housing, and fair wages. Not to mention, they’re facing one of the harshest summers to date due to climate change._

**Protecting our migrant workers protects our economy.**

As Americans, we should be appalled by this interference and have to continue to spread the message to the democrat voters.
**This is why it is more important to make your voices heard at the ballot box this November and this August at the Primary. There are no excuses.**
Republicans are the party of the people and the Every Day American. This is your fight to save our democracy and our country and **the** **time is NOW**.

| | By now I'm sure you've seen the news that President Joe Biden has made the decision to withdraw his candidacy for President of the United States. I've been proud to work with President Biden on a record number of Democratic successes these past three-and-a-half years. From the bipartisan infrastructure bill to the CHIPS Act to the historic Inflation Reduction Act, under President Biden's leadership, Democrats have gained enormous ground in the fight to hold Big Pharma accountable and set us on course to a clean energy future. We've also made major gains in the fights against wealthy tax cheats, and in tackling the climate crisis head-on. I have no doubt that history will judge well those landmark achievements. I support the President's decision to withdraw his candidacy, and ultimately believe it is the best decision for the future of our country, and our party. [**That's why I'm also proud to announce that I'm all in to support Vice President Kamala Harris to build on that impressive record and defeat Donald Trump this November. Kamala's candidacy is nothing short of historic. I know firsthand from my time serving with her in the Senate that she is a staunch defender of working families, and someone we can always count on to hold big corporations and special interests accountable. She's a proven defender of reproductive freedom and our most essential liberties. She has always been on the frontlines of every effort to level the playing field for the American people, and **I believe she is the right choice to lead our party – and our country – into a new era of leadership that will build on the progress Democrats have made.**
I know the next few months aren't going to be easy. Democrats will be fighting an uphill battle against convicted felon Donald Trump and a united MAGA Republican Party, who want to yank America backward with his checkered and erratic past of right-wing extremism on women's health care, dirty energy and more.
**Our grassroots movement has defeated Donald Trump and his extremist agenda before, and I know we can do it again. But we won't be able to do it without your support.**[**So please join me in this fight to elect an unapologetically pro-choice, progressive leader to the White House this November – split a donation today >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89366667/487063182/-118994385?refcode=2024-07-22-harris&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=ee7604b6-7d48-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZTc2MDRiNi03ZDQ4LWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wLBHnVmi_5L1lE878ylwVAJNSN6oLHziA1osE2hSOp0=)
Time before Election Day might be in short supply, but the dedication and motivation of our movement is not. So I hope you'll join me in the fight to elect a president who will work for working families, not special interests. In my view, that person is Kamala Harris.
Onward,
_Ron_

clean_body: | | | | By now I'm sure you've seen the news that President Joe Biden has made the decision to withdraw his candidacy for President of the United States. I've been proud to work with President Biden on a record number of Democratic successes these past three-and-a-half years. From the bipartisan infrastructure bill to the CHIPS Act to the historic Inflation Reduction Act, under President Biden's leadership, Democrats have gained enormous ground in the fight to hold Big Pharma accountable and set us on course to a clean energy future. We've also made major gains in the fights against wealthy tax cheats, and in tackling the climate crisis head-on. I have no doubt that history will judge well those landmark achievements. I support the President's decision to withdraw his candidacy, and ultimately believe it is the best decision for the future of our country, and our party. = Donate Now If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly and split it between Kamala Harris and Ron Wyden: | = | = ---|--- = | = = Kamala's candidacy is nothing short of historic. I know firsthand from my time serving with her in the Senate that she is a staunch defender of working families, and someone we can always count on to hold big corporations and special interests accountable. She's a proven defender of reproductive freedom and our most essential liberties. She has always been on the frontlines of every effort to level the playing field for the American people, and I believe she is the right choice to lead our party – and our country – into a new era of leadership that will build on the progress Democrats have made. I know the next few months aren't going to be easy. Democrats will be fighting an uphill battle against convicted felon Donald Trump and a united MAGA Republican Party, who want to yank America backward with his checkered and erratic past of right-wing extremism on women's health care, dirty energy and more. Our grassroots movement has defeated Donald Trump and his extremist agenda before, and I know we can do it again. But we won't be able to do it without your support.= Time before Election Day might be in short supply, but the dedication and motivation of our movement is not. So I hope you'll join me in the fight to elect a president who will work for working families, not special interests. In my view, that person is Kamala Harris. Back in 2020, the Biden-Harris team won over a lot of Veterans who voted for Republicans in the past.

Having a Veteran on the ticket could keep that momentum going. It enhances our chances of winning.

name: Rep. Joe Sweeney
subject: Cut through the noise: Time to Focus.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Granite Solutions, Joe Sweeney Chairman
body:
Vote Republican Up and Down the Ballot.
| | | |
---
| Dear Derek,
A lot of news has been made in the last few weeks, but I wanted to make sure you saw my latest op-ed in the New Hampshire Union Leader:
_"But this election isn’t just about the presidency. It’s vital that we vote Republican up and down the ballot to continue the policies that have brought success to our state and country. Here in New Hampshire, we’ve seen the tangible benefits of Republican leadership. We have reduced our state’s debt by 25-30% without depleting our rainy day fund, and we’ve attracted major developments like Tuscan Village and businesses like New Balance, creating thousands of high-paying jobs and expanding our economy.
_ _
_**_We know that when the government gets out of the way and enables people to do more and be more, that we all get to achieve more, and that’s the Republican promise for 2025 and beyond._** _
__We need to keep this momentum going by electing strong Republican candidates at every level of government. Our state’s future depends on maintaining a pro-business environment, supporting our local economies, and ensuring our communities stay safe and prosperous. The Democrat Party, mired in internal conflict and led by an increasingly unpopular president, offers little in the way of solutions. Their policies have failed to meet the needs of everyday Americans."_
**Read the full Op-Ed here:[https://www.unionleader.com/opinion/op-eds/rep-joe-sweeney-love-nh-vote-republican-up-and-down-the-ballot-next-fall/article_b0f39c48-4509-11ef-b10d-d322ec1228a6.html ](https://link.emails.granitesolutions.)**
Best,
Joe
Rep. Joe Sweeney Chairman & Founder, Granite Solutions

body:
and our role in helping her win Michigan
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1681%2E135344%2Eo7q_rw)

Friend --
We all know that our country is going through a period of political change right now. The last few weeks alone have had enough unprecedented events to last a lifetime, and very few Americans want it this way.
But it highlights something fundamental: there’s so much at stake this November, and in the face of the extreme Project 2025 agenda, it’s imperative that we be focused and united.
Vice President Kamala Harris has taken on Big Pharma, helped usher in a manufacturing renaissance in Michigan, and fought to protect our rights and our democracy.
I support Vice President Harris as she unites not only our party, but also our country to defeat Donald Trump.
But here’s what this change means for our campaigns: in order to make her our next President -- and hold on to the U.S. Senate -- we have to keep Michigan blue. It’s just about as simple as that. Period. Full Stop.
If that is all you need to hear, I hope you’ll use this link to split a donation between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Kamala Harris’ campaign for President:
**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ebs-em-harris-july24](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-harris-july24.TaFOzz&refcode=em240722-3-900&t=2&akid=1681%2E135344%2Eo7q_rw)**
But if there is more you need to hear, I would love to explain.
This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state.
Add to that the fact that, while most people know who Vice President Harris is, we need to spend the next three months reintroducing her as our nominee and highlighting why she is the right choice in the November election.
Because Michigan is a swing state, our race will likely impact the presidential and vice versa. That means everything we do in our race has the power to influence races up and down the ballot. In order to secure the White House for Kamala Harris, our Senate campaign has to perform well on Election Day.
We’re in a unique situation, with a lot of work to do before Election Day to ensure we keep Michigan blue.
[**So that’s why I ask: will you split a $5 donation between my campaign and Kamala Harris’? It has never been more important to be unified in pursuit of a common goal.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-harris-july24.TaFOzz&refcode=em240722-3-900&t=3&akid=1681%2E135344%2Eo7q_rw)

The American people deserve answers, Fellow American.

**_Ten days after the attempted assassination of President Trump’s life, the Secret Service refuses to answer questions._**

_**First**_ – the Secret Service Director’s opening statements were leaked to several Democrat-run publications.

_**Then**_ – the Secret Service Director was subpoenaed by Congress and failed to answer even the simplest of “yes” and “no” questions on if they failed.

_**Now**_ – a protective government agency, that is not supposed to be political, is dragging its feet about generating a report on how the Secret Service did not live up to its “no fail” mission.

**_It is complete and utter bull****, and I made sure to tell that to Director Cheatle._**

With the election only 100 days out, this is unacceptable.

**_The American people deserve answers, and we deserve them now!_**

| | **From the Chairman**
---
| | If you needed any further evidence of China’s global ambitions, have a read of the Communist Party’s recently [released](http://links.rogersforsenate.com/u/click?_t=b90de78796ce4ce596523293a2b8ff82&_m=023df670b2024182a3fa2e161fa4da39&_e=nTWMNK5l3NuUwsMivrf1NLDLYxEwlPAedbRnSvvylHaiHzzJNzRfn4189aRHaQRpYY0bFv-hN-liM7XR5LNOkRF1tzct5hsXETuq5ehevgoqxXsHb1zfS3JrZnCvC4mjC_XCDdStLW5_kt3f_5R_7hH3PoaRoIcQlde54wvVv87ZDmUYo5NvCOBRzx1JFIWuGKIaS_x7j-Xwq1wDtmVhSoz7vAfCsDBLJj-2Tb75ROTsYKg4AKfndzvIIXnK2BtE7D1Nbme_pgoKvsRmSXnwDROS80IbJJtcqc0IPX864FxtQkqeKK3WZGbbtTlH-Vgl) 50-page roadmap that came out of its recent meeting. Containing some 300 reforms, the plan aims to solidify the Party’s ambitions to make China a global technological and economic powerhouse and shore up growing weaknesses within its domestic market. Greater emphasis is placed on national security as Beijing is widening definitions of what constitutes a risk to the Party and the country, making it more difficult for foreign businesses to work in the country. China is authoritarian full stop, but it is an adaptable authoritarian state—it responds to domestic pressures and international actions. What does this mean for America? It means we need smart policies that put pressure on Beijing, dissuade it from harming our interests, and deter it from acting against our allies. This is a constant process that demands smart and strong leadership that will stand up to the Chinese Communist Party. We need that now more than ever.

subject: My endorsement for President
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warnock for Georgia, Title and affiliation are provided for identification purposes only
body:
Let’s win this – together.
Let’s win this – together.
| | |
---
Friend,

President Joe Biden demonstrated again this weekend that he is a selfless servant leader and a true patriot, and why he is one of the most effective Presidents of my lifetime. Joe Biden has always put the people first.

He put the people first when he passed critical Covid relief necessary to get our families and communities through a once-in-a-century pandemic. He put the people first when he signed into law the largest middle and working class tax cut in American history. He put the people first when he invested in manufacturing and clean energy, and found a way to offer student debt relief for millions of Americans. name: Joe Biden
subject: I'm endorsing Kamala Harris to be the next President of the United States.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Biden for President
body:
| | |
---
My fellow Americans, Over the past three and a half years, we have made great progress as a nation. Today, America has the strongest economy in the world. We've made historic investments in rebuilding our nation, in lowering prescription drug costs for seniors, and in expanding affordable health care to a record number of Americans. We've provided critically needed care to a million veterans exposed to toxic substances. Passed the first gun safety law in 30 years. Appointed the first African American woman to the Supreme Court. And passed the most significant climate legislation in the history of the world. America has never been better positioned to lead than we are today. I know none of this could have been done without you, the American people. Together, we overcame a once in a century pandemic and the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression. We've protected and preserved our democracy. And we've revitalized and strengthened our alliances around the world. It has been the greatest honor of my life to serve as your President. And while it has been my intention to seek reelection, I believe it is in the best interest of my party and the country for me to stand down and to focus solely on fulfilling my duties as President for the remainder of my term. For my part: my very first decision as the party nominee in 2020 was to pick Kamala Harris as my Vice President. And it’s been the best decision I’ve made. **I want to offer my full support and endorsement for Kamala to be the nominee of our party this year. clean_body: | | | My fellow Americans, Over the past three and a half years, we have made great progress as a nation. Today, America has the strongest economy in the world. We've made historic investments in rebuilding our nation, in lowering prescription drug costs for seniors, and in expanding affordable health care to a record number of Americans. We've provided critically needed care to a million veterans exposed to toxic substances. Passed the first gun safety law in 30 years. Appointed the first African American woman to the Supreme Court. And passed the most significant climate legislation in the history of the world. America has never been better positioned to lead than we are today. I know none of this could have been done without you, the American people. Together, we overcame a once in a century pandemic and the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression. We've protected and preserved our democracy. And we've revitalized and strengthened our alliances around the world. It has been the greatest honor of my life to serve as your President. And while it has been my intention to seek reelection, I believe it is in the best interest of my party and the country for me to stand down and to focus solely on fulfilling my duties as President for the remainder of my term. For my part: my very first decision as the party nominee in 2020 was to pick Kamala Harris as my Vice President. And it’s been the best decision I’ve made. I want to offer my full support and endorsement for Kamala to be the nominee of our party this year. # Join River: Fight for Progress and Justice
---
| President Joe Biden has shown us what **true** leadership looks like—compassion, dedication, and resilience. I thank him for his more than 50 years of public service to our country.
---
| **Here’s how he’s impacted our lives:**
---
|
* **Reproductive Freedom** : Standing firm on women's rights and expanding access to reproductive healthcare.
* **Water Conservation** : Initiating policies to protect our natural resources and address climate change.
* **Healthcare Access** : Strengthening and expanding the Affordable Care Act.
* **Infrastructure** : Investing in modern, sustainable infrastructure to benefit future generations.

---
| I stand by President Biden in his [endorsement](https://rivergassenforcongress.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=3a7f5669b9b38d0a59e26b798&id=7e115892a6&e=3818d77efc) for Vice President Harris and I will stand behind whomever is selected at next month’s Democratic National Convention.
---
|
